title: Grade 9: Explore and build habits
steps: Build strong study habits and aim for your best grades from day one
Read widely and begin practicing English daily (books, podcasts, writing)
Try new clubs, sports and subjects to see what you enjoy
Start a simple journal of what you like and what you are good at

title: Grade 10: Go deeper
steps: Join one or two activities seriously and aim for a role or responsibility
Volunteer or start a small project that helps your community
Learn what degrees and careers exist in the fields you like
Talk to women working in careers that interest you

title: Grade 11: Research and prepare
steps: Research countries, universities and the costs of studying there
List scholarships, their deadlines and requirements
Choose and prepare for an English test: IELTS, TOEFL or Duolingo English Test
Check whether your target schools need SAT/ACT or other exams, or are test-optional
Ask teachers who know you well whether they would write recommendation letters

title: Grade 12: Apply
steps: Make a shortlist of 6 to 10 schools: some reach, some match, some safe
Draft your personal essay early and ask someone to review it
Collect transcripts, certificates and recommendation letters
Track every deadline in one calendar or spreadsheet
Apply for scholarships alongside your university applications

title: After admission: Prepare to move
steps: Compare offers and financial aid, then accept one by the deadline
Apply for your student visa and gather financial documents
Arrange housing, insurance and travel
Connect with student groups from your country before you arrive
